newsitem.title: FINLAND: EMU report does not change govt stance -Lipponen.
newsitem.headline: EMU report does not change govt stance -Lipponen.

text.p: Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Wednesday that an EMU report by an expert group did not give reason for the government to reconsider its objective that Finland should join the single currency from start.

Asked by a Reuters reporter whether the findings of the report by a government-appointed expert panel led by economics professor Jukka Pekkarinen gave reason for the government to reconsider its EMU stance, Lipponen said: "Certainly not."
The not yet published EMU report was reviewed on Wednesday at a meeting of the economic council, a discussion forum led by the prime minister and grouping top economic decision makers.

Lipponen repeated that the report, which is scheduled for release on May 6, did not contain any recommendation whether or not Finland should join the third stage of European economic and monetary union, slated for start-up in January 1999.
The left-right-green government's stated target is that Finland should meet all EMU entry criteria to be able to join the single currency in the first group.

Parliament will have the final say. A vote on participation is due in spring 1998 before a scheduled summit of European Union heads of state and government, which is due to make the final decision on which countries will join EMU from day one.
